newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NATO-RUSSIA PACT DISPELS ASPIRANTS' FEARS-HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: NATO-RUSSIA PACT DISPELS ASPIRANTS' FEARS-HUNGARY.

text.p: Hungary welcomed a historic NATO-Russia security pact signed on Tuesday in Paris saying it dispelled concerns about possible second-class membership of NATO hopefuls.

"We especially welcome the fact that the document does not contain any committment on NATO's part that would restrict the rights of new entrants, or would lead to some form of 'second-class' membership," Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi told a news conference.
NATO leaders and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed on Tuesday the Founding Act on Mutual Relations desgined to bind Russia into efforts to create a new European security order.

"This is a compromise that does not hurt the medium or long-term interests of either side," Szentivanyi said, adding that Hungary has always given "due consideration" to Russia's justified security interests.
NATO is expected to issue the first invitations to prospective new members -- expected to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- at a summit in the Spanish capital Madrid in July.
